images.title: Copy in any direction
images.purpose: Show an angle copied onto a ray pointing in a quite different direction, with the same radius and the same chord.
images.composition: The given angle on the left opening to the right; its copy on the right turned to open downwards and to the left; a wide gap between them.
exact_structure: Left: a vertex A with two dark arms opening to the right, about 50° apart; a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at A cuts the arms at B and C; a thin dashed amber (#E69F00) chord BC.
Right: a dark ray from X pointing down and to the left; a grey (#6B7280) arc centred at X, of the same radius as at A, cuts the ray at Z.
Right: a small grey (#6B7280) arc centred at Z, of radius BC, cuts the first arc at Y; a thin dashed amber (#E69F00) chord ZY.
Right: a reddish purple (#CC79A7) ray from X through Y, the copied arm.
Both angles carry one small reddish purple (#CC79A7) angle arc of the same size at the vertex.
No numbers and no protractor anywhere.
rejection: the copied angle visibly larger or smaller than the given angle
the copy facing the same direction as the given angle
the arc at X drawn with a different radius from the arc at A, or chord ZY a different length from BC
images.takeaway: A copied angle can point any way; equal radius and equal chord still make the triangles congruent by SSS.
images.description: An angle at A opening right and its copy at X turned to open down and left, each with a grey arc and an equal amber dashed chord.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the two amber chords and the two grey arcs, then say the SSS reason the angles match.

image_decisions.why: Showing a copy in a new orientation is the exact skill the practice asks for.
